html:
The Kogi, who call themselves Kággaba, are an Indigenous people of the northern slopes of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in Colombia, the highest coastal mountain range in the world.

They speak a Chibchan language and see themselves, with the Arhuaco, Wiwa and Kankuamo, as heirs of the Tairona, whose stone towns such as Ciudad Perdida lie in the same forests. Their priests, the mamos, are trained from childhood, by tradition spending years in darkness to learn to see the spiritual world. The Kogi farm small plots at several altitudes and keep themselves apart from outsiders.

The Kogi withdrew into the mountains after Spanish attacks in the 1500s and 1600s. In 1990 they invited a BBC film crew to film "From the Heart of the World", a warning to the "younger brothers" of the outside world that they were destroying the Earth.
sum: The Kogi, who call themselves Kággaba, are an Indigenous people of the northern slopes of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in Colombia, the highest coastal mountain range in the world.
